title: merge, join and concat: keys, cardinality and the rows that duplicated

videos.script: The trips know a station's code. They do not know its name. {{code}} The days know how many trips they had. They do not know how much it rained. {{days}} Every answer that needs both tables needs a join. {{join}} pandas calls it merge. It pairs each row with the rows on the other side whose key is equal. {{merge}} Most of the time that is all there is to it. {{simple}} This lesson is about the other times. A trip with no end station, dropped by the default. {{dropped}} A station with two names, so every trip from it comes out twice. Thirty-three thousand trips go in, and almost thirty-six thousand rows come out. {{twice}} A key typed with a space at the end, matching nothing. {{space}} None of them raises an error. So the habit is simple. Count the rows before the join, and count them after. {{end}}
